summary:
New A1/A2 boundary this turn — who actually executes an incoming heartbeat — recorded as a source assessment with an explicit feasibility boundary (valid:true).

Sourced behaviours promoted. An AppendEntries is classified as a heartbeat purely by field shape on the receiving side (non-zero term, leader address present, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero, no entries, LeaderCommitIndex zero; net_transport.go:656-690); when a heartbeat handler is registered the transport calls it directly in the connection goroutine and never hands the RPC to the consumer channel (net_transport.go:718-740), and Raft registers processHeartbeat for that callback (api.go:610-620), which checks shutdown and the command type and then calls the same appendEntries the run loop uses (raft.go:1415-1440). For that shape the reachable mutations are narrow and all synchronised: the older-term branch returns without touching state, a newer term or the non-follower sentinel does setState(Follower) plus setCurrentTerm, the leader address/ID are recorded under leaderLock, success sets last contact under its own lock, and the previous-log check, entry loop, configuration processing and commit-index update are all skipped because PrevLogEntry, the entry list and LeaderCommitIndex are zero — with raftState documented as thread safe and storing term/commit/applied atomically plus snapshot/log indexes under lastLock (state.go:44-77). The leader's heartbeat goroutine deliberately sends only header, term and leader fields with no commit index (replication.go:383-425), so followers learn the commit index through the replicate loop's CommitTimeout path instead; and the ordinary replicate path cannot take the fast path because it sets LeaderCommitIndex and a previous log entry. The in-memory transport explicitly declines the fast path (inmem_transport.go:72-78).

Conclusion recorded as explained with no defect claim: the fast path's safety rests on the request shape confining reachable mutations plus every reachable mutation being lock- or atomic-protected, and the classification being unreachable from the ordinary replication producers in this revision. Two boundaries are stated rather than glossed over: no interleaving proof is attempted, and the path could not be executed here at all — the fast path exists only on the network transport and this run's execution isolation has no network namespace, so a clean local race-detector run of two in-memory cluster harnesses is explicitly recorded as not being evidence about it.
